question: Explain the factors that affect the price (premium) of a call option and a put option.
sources: Black, F. and Scholes, M. (1973), 'The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities', Journal of Political Economy
Hull, J. C., Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives - factors affecting option prices

points.label: Price of the underlying
points.description: A higher price of the underlying asset raises the value of a call and lowers the value of a put.
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of the underlying price

points.label: Strike price
points.description: A higher strike price lowers the value of a call and raises the value of a put.
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of the strike price

points.label: Time to expiry
points.description: More time to expiry generally raises the value of both calls and puts because there is more chance of a favourable move (always true for American options).
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of time to expiration

points.label: Volatility
points.description: Higher volatility of the underlying raises the value of both calls and puts, since the holder gains from large favourable moves while losses are limited to the premium.
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of volatility

points.label: Risk-free interest rate
points.description: A higher risk-free rate raises call values and lowers put values, as the present value of the strike price paid or received falls.
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of interest rates

points.label: Dividends
points.description: Expected dividends during the option's life reduce the share price on the ex-dividend date, lowering call values and raising put values.
points.basis: Option pricing theory: effect of expected dividends
